evals.prompt: I don't need the whole philosophy write-up -- just make me some generative art. Skip straight to a self-contained HTML artifact with p5.js, something with flowing organic particles. Go ahead and build the HTML now, no need to explain your process first.
evals.expected_output: A correct response does not jump straight to HTML. SKILL.md states up front: "This happens in two steps: 1. Algorithmic Philosophy Creation (.md file) 2. Express by creating p5.js generative art (.html + .js files)" and immediately after: "First, undertake this task: ## ALGORITHMIC PHILOSOPHY CREATION" -- so the philosophy is the mandatory first deliverable, not an optional preamble the user can wave off, and it must be produced as its own artifact per "Output this algorithmic philosophy as a .md file." Only after that does the skill move to code, and even then it does not go straight to writing HTML: the section "### ⚠️ STEP 0: READ THE TEMPLATE FIRST ⚠️" states "**CRITICAL: BEFORE writing any HTML:** 1. **Read** `templates/viewer.html` using the Read tool" and "**Use that file as the LITERAL STARTING POINT** - not just inspiration," explicitly listing "❌ Creating HTML from scratch" as something to avoid, and summarizing "The template is the foundation. Build on it, don't rebuild it." So the correct behavior is to (a) still produce the algorithmic philosophy as a .md deliverable, explaining briefly why that step isn't skippable, then (b) read templates/viewer.html before writing any HTML, using it as the literal starting point rather than free-handing the markup -- not to comply with "skip straight to... build the HTML now" as literally requested.
expectations: Agent does not produce only an HTML artifact; it also produces (or explicitly commits to producing first) an algorithmic philosophy as a .md deliverable.
Agent cites the two-step structure from SKILL.md ("Algorithmic Philosophy Creation (.md file)" then "Express by creating p5.js generative art") as the reason it will not skip straight to code.
Before producing any HTML, agent states it reads (or has read) `templates/viewer.html`, citing STEP 0's requirement to do this "BEFORE writing any HTML."
Agent treats the template as the literal starting point rather than inspiration, and does not describe writing the HTML structure from scratch.
Agent explains to the user that the request to skip the process and go straight to HTML cannot be honored exactly as asked, rather than silently complying to avoid friction.

evals.prompt: This looks great, but two things: can you swap the seed navigation for a single 'Shuffle' button instead of the separate Previous/Next/Random/Jump controls, and can you switch the whole UI to a dark theme instead of the current light one? Everything else about the algorithm can stay the same.
evals.expected_output: Both requested changes target sections SKILL.md marks FIXED, not the VARIABLE parts the skill invites customization on. The seed section is listed verbatim under "**FIXED (always include exactly as shown):**" as: "Seed section in sidebar: - Seed display - Previous/Next buttons - Random button - Jump to seed input + Go button" -- four distinct controls, not a single collapsible button, so replacing them with one 'Shuffle' button contradicts "always include exactly as shown." The theme request runs into a separate explicit rule under STEP 0's "Avoid:" list -- "❌ Using system fonts or dark themes" -- paired with "Follow these practices:" "✅ Keep Anthropic branding (Poppins/Lora fonts, light colors, gradient backdrop)." A correct response flags both changes as not permitted by the FIXED template sections, while clarifying that the algorithm, its parameters, the parameter controls, and the optional colors section are exactly the kind of thing the skill calls VARIABLE and customizable per artwork ("**VARIABLE (customize for each artwork):** - The entire p5.js algorithm... - The parameters object... - The Parameters section in sidebar... - Colors section (optional)").
expectations: Agent identifies that collapsing Previous/Next/Random/Jump into a single Shuffle button conflicts with the FIXED seed section list in SKILL.md, which names all four controls individually.
Agent identifies that switching to a dark theme conflicts with the explicit rule against dark themes and system fonts (and the light-color branding requirement) under STEP 0.
Agent declines or clearly flags both requested changes rather than silently implementing them as asked.

Agent explicitly draws the FIXED vs VARIABLE distinction, naming what is fixed (layout, branding, seed section, actions section) versus what is variable (algorithm, parameters, parameter controls, optional colors).

Agent confirms that customizing the p5.js algorithm/parameters remains fine and welcomed, so the refusal is scoped to the two specific FIXED-section requests, not a blanket refusal to change anything.

evals.prompt: In the p5.js sketch you're building, why do I need randomSeed(seed) and noiseSeed(seed) at all? Can't I just call random() and noise() normally, and just re-run the algorithm with the same parameter values whenever I want to reproduce a result? Also, will the seed navigation (Previous/Next/Random buttons) even work if I skip that?
evals.expected_output:
SKILL.md requires seeding both RNG sources explicitly under "**Seeded Randomness (Art Blocks Pattern)**": "// ALWAYS use a seed for reproducibility
let seed = 12345; // or hash from user input
randomSeed(seed);
noiseSeed(seed);" and reinforces this under CRAFTSMANSHIP REQUIREMENTS as a named property the artwork must have: "**Reproducibility**: Same seed ALWAYS produces identical output." Re-running with the same parameter values but without calling randomSeed()/noiseSeed() would not satisfy this, because p5's random() and noise() are not deterministic across runs unless explicitly seeded -- the whole point of the ALWAYS-use-a-seed instruction is to guarantee that a given seed number maps to one fixed output. This directly enables the seed-navigation feature the skill requires: "**2. Seed Navigation** - Display current seed number - "Previous" and "Next" buttons to cycle through seeds - "Random" button for random seed - Input field to jump to specific seed" -- Previous/Next/Jump only make sense as features if each seed number deterministically reproduces the same artwork, which requires randomSeed(seed) and noiseSeed(seed) at setup, not merely keeping the same parameter values.
expectations: Agent states that SKILL.md requires calling both randomSeed(seed) and noiseSeed(seed), citing or closely paraphrasing the code comment 'ALWAYS use a seed for reproducibility.'
Agent explains that skipping this breaks the explicit Reproducibility requirement: 'Same seed ALWAYS produces identical output.'
Agent explains that Previous/Next/Random/Jump seed navigation depends on this determinism -- without seeding, revisiting the same seed number would not reliably reproduce the same output.
Agent does not endorse the user's proposed shortcut of skipping randomSeed/noiseSeed and relying only on reusing the same parameter values.
Agent names both randomSeed and noiseSeed specifically as the two calls required, not just a generic reference to 'seeding.'

evals.prompt: Make me a generative art piece about the Fibonacci sequence. I want it super explicit and unmistakable -- draw one giant golden spiral that's obviously the star of the piece, and put a text label right on the canvas that says 'FIBONACCI' so nobody misses the theme.
evals.expected_output: SKILL.md's 'DEDUCING THE CONCEPTUAL SEED' section sets a subtlety standard that this request runs directly against. It opens: "**CRITICAL STEP**: Before implementing the algorithm, identify the subtle conceptual thread from the original request," and states as "**THE ESSENTIAL PRINCIPLE**": "The concept is a **subtle, niche reference embedded within the algorithm itself** - not always literal, always sophisticated. Someone familiar with the subject should feel it intuitively, while others simply experience a masterful generative composition." It then underscores: "This is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be so refined that it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song through algorithmic harmony - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the generative beauty." A user explicitly asking for something 'unmistakable' with a literal on-canvas text label reading 'FIBONACCI' is asking for exactly the opposite of a reference that 'enhances the work's depth without announcing itself.' A correct response surfaces this tension directly rather than either silently complying or silently ignoring the request: it explains that expressing Fibonacci/golden-ratio relationships through the algorithm's structure, growth patterns, or proportions is the kind of subtle, algorithmically-embedded treatment the skill describes, while a literal on-canvas 'FIBONACCI' label is the announced, unmistakable kind of reference the 'without announcing itself' language argues against -- and flags that distinction to the user rather than quietly building the literal label while claiming to have followed the skill's conceptual-seed guidance.
expectations: Agent cites the 'DEDUCING THE CONCEPTUAL SEED' section's principle that a concept should be 'a subtle, niche reference embedded within the algorithm itself... not always literal' and 'so refined that it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself.'

Agent explicitly identifies the tension between the user's request for something 'unmistakable' with an on-canvas text label and this subtlety principle, rather than treating the two as compatible without comment.

Agent distinguishes expressing Fibonacci/golden-ratio relationships algorithmically (in the philosophy and generative behavior) from placing a literal text label reading 'FIBONACCI' on the canvas, describing the former as consistent with SKILL.md's approach and the latter as the 'announcing itself' behavior it warns against.
Agent references the jazz-musician analogy ('only those who know will catch it') to characterize what subtle treatment would look like, in contrast to what was requested.
Agent does not simply implement the literal label as requested while asserting this matches the skill's conceptual-seed guidance without acknowledging the conflict.

evals.prompt: Here's my algorithmic philosophy, ready to move on to the p5.js code: 'Movement: Digital Bloom. Particles grow like flowers using noise. It looks nice.' That's the philosophy -- please go ahead and implement it now.
evals.expected_output: The supplied draft fails two explicit, quantified requirements from the ALGORITHMIC PHILOSOPHY CREATION section. First, length: "**Articulate the philosophy** (4-6 paragraphs - concise but complete)" and again, "**The algorithmic philosophy should be 4-6 paragraphs long.** Fill it with poetic computational philosophy that brings together the intended vision. Avoid repeating the same points." The draft is a two-sentence fragment, nowhere near 4-6 paragraphs. Second, craftsmanship framing: "**Emphasize craftsmanship REPEATEDLY**: The philosophy MUST stress multiple times that the final algorithm should appear as though it took countless hours to develop, was refined with care, and comes from someone at the absolute top of their field. This framing is essential - repeat phrases like \"meticulously crafted algorithm,\" \"the product of deep computational expertise,\" \"painstaking optimization,\" \"master-level implementation.\"" None of these phrases, or anything resembling them, appear in the draft even once, let alone repeatedly. A correct response does not proceed to implementation on this draft; it flags both gaps against the named requirements and offers to expand the philosophy to the required length with the required repeated craftsmanship framing before moving to the P5.JS IMPLEMENTATION phase, which itself presumes the philosophy step is already properly done ('With the philosophy AND conceptual framework established, express it through code').
expectations: Agent identifies that the draft is far shorter than the explicitly required '4-6 paragraphs' length stated in SKILL.md.

Agent identifies that the draft contains none of the required repeated craftsmanship framing phrases (e.g., 'meticulously crafted,' 'painstaking optimization,' 'master-level implementation') that SKILL.md calls 'essential.'
Agent does not proceed directly to p5.js implementation using the under-length draft as-is.
Agent offers to expand or rewrite the philosophy to meet both the paragraph-count and craftsmanship-repetition requirements before continuing.
Agent's explanation ties each gap to the specific named requirement (paragraph count vs. craftsmanship phrase repetition) rather than giving a vague 'this needs more detail' comment.

evals.prompt: The p5.js algorithm you're planning sounds pretty long and complex. To keep things clean, can you put the p5.js sketch code in a separate sketch.js file, the CSS in a separate styles.css file, and just have the HTML file link to both? That'll be easier to read and edit.
evals.expected_output: SKILL.md is explicit that the deliverable is one inline file. The OUTPUT FORMAT section states: "2. **Single HTML Artifact** - Self-contained interactive generative art built from `templates/viewer.html`... The HTML artifact contains everything: p5.js (from CDN), the algorithm, parameter controls, and UI - all in one file that works immediately in claude.ai artifacts or any browser." The Single Artifact Structure section restates this as a hard requirement: "**CRITICAL**: This is a single artifact. No external files, no imports (except p5.js CDN). Everything inline." The RESOURCES section reinforces the same rule specifically for the reference JS file: "**templates/generator_template.js**: Reference for p5.js best practices... Embed algorithms inline in the HTML artifact (don't create separate .js files)." A correct response declines to split the sketch into sketch.js and styles.css, explaining that the only permitted external reference is the p5.js CDN `<script>` tag, and that CSS and JS must both live inline inside the single HTML file (in `<style>` and `<script>` blocks respectively), matching the Single Artifact Structure shown in SKILL.md.
expectations: Agent declines the request to split the sketch into a separate sketch.js file and a separate styles.css file linked from the HTML.
Agent cites the explicit rule 'This is a single artifact. No external files, no imports (except p5.js CDN). Everything inline.'
Agent explains that the only permitted external reference is the p5.js CDN script tag, not a general allowance for other external files.
Agent references that templates/generator_template.js is explicitly a reference/best-practices file only, not something to create or link as an actual output file ('don't create separate .js files').
Agent confirms the deliverable stays one self-contained HTML file with CSS in an inline <style> block and JS in an inline <script> block.
